capability: The main navigation bar's keyboard focus indicator on any ToggleButton.nav is visibly rendered on screen and distinguishable from the selected-page underline in both the light and dark themes without ever hiding that underline on a tab that is both selected and focused, and startup keyboard focus lands on the selected page's own navigation tab instead of always Home
searchEvidence: docs/handoff/bugs/BUG-20260926-nav-focus-looks-selected.md and docs/handoff/1.1.12.md owner decision 32 (full text): 'only the selected page's navigation tab shows the blue underline. Keyboard focus stays visible but must not look like selection, and startup focus goes to the selected page's tab instead of always Home.' The first R1 pass in this record covered only the shape/underline clause; the commander relayed the owner's decision that the startup-focus-target clause is in scope for this same task, so the record and implementation are redone before any push to cover all three clauses together.

rg -n 'ToggleButton.nav' src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/Styles/MainWindowStyles.axaml: ToggleButton.nav:checked draws BorderThickness 0,0,0,2 in NfcAccentBrush on the ContentPresenter (the only 'selected' indicator); ToggleButton.nav:focus-visible drew the identical BorderThickness 0,0,0,2 shape in NfcAccentBorderStrongBrush, so focus and selection differed only by color, never by shape.

rg -n 'focus-visible' src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/Styles: every other control whose non-focused state already owns a directional or absent border (Button.settingsNavItem, the generic Button:focus-visible rule shared with RadioButton.messageCenterNavigationItem/activityFilter, ToggleButton.slotStateAction, ToggleButton.quietDisclosure, Border.memoryCoverageLinkedRow) draws :focus-visible as a full uniform BorderThickness 2 outline, never reusing the selected/checked shape; this is the repo's one existing focus-visible convention for controls with a distinct selected look. It does not cover a control whose selected state must stay visible while also focused, which is ToggleButton.nav's actual requirement (see the independent review below).

src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/Styles/ThemeTokens.axaml: in the Dark theme dictionary, NfcAccentBrush and NfcAccentBorderStrongBrush both resolve to #60A5FA (identical color), so relying on color alone can never distinguish focus from selection in dark mode; only a distinct rendering channel, not just a distinct color, can.

src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/MainWindow.axaml.cs PresentPreloadStage/CommitRequiredStagePresentation: after the required history stage succeeds, restoreFocus() unconditionally posted HomeNavigationButton.Focus(NavigationMethod.Tab), regardless of viewModel.SelectedPage. src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/MainWindow.Report.cs ApplyLaunchPage runs earlier in the same required-stage work (before the succeeded/restoreFocus callback, confirmed by XamlControlStyleContractTests.Startup's existing launch-before-concurrent ordering assertion) and already executes ShowMergeCommand/ShowReplaceCommand from UiLaunchOptions' '--page' value, so viewModel.SelectedPage reliably reflects the launch target by the time focus is restored.

src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/ViewModels/MainWindowViewModel.Navigation.cs PageLabel(ShellPage) is the repo's existing convention for switching on the internal ShellPage enum (Home, Merge, Replace, HexEditor): a block-bodied method returning a fully populated switch expression with an explicit arm per enum member. The new SelectedNavigationButton(MainWindowViewModel) helper in MainWindow.axaml.cs follows the same shape (dotnet build enforces it: IDE0022 rejected an expression-bodied member and IDE0072 rejected an unpopulated switch). HexEditor has no nav tab, so it falls back to HomeNavigationButton, unchanged from the previous always-Home behavior for that one page.

Independent read-only review (codex/gpt-6-sol) of exact head 6dee964a0 found F-1 [P2]: making :focus-visible override the same ContentPresenter's BorderBrush/BorderThickness that :checked sets means a tab that is both selected and focused (the normal startup case, since startup focus now lands on the selected page) shows only the focus outline and loses its required blue underline, violating decision 32's first clause. rg -n 'BoxShadow' src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/Styles found an existing, already-themed token pattern (NfcWorkflowCardHoverShadow, NfcWorkflowCardPressedShadow) for a BoxShadow that renders independently of BorderBrush/BorderThickness on the same element; ContentPresenter exposes a BoxShadow property (confirmed by reflecting Avalonia.Controls.Presenters.ContentPresenter, Avalonia 12.0.5). rg -n 'focus-within' src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia also found an existing two-element overlay precedent (Border.versionSourceEditor:focus-within reacting to a focused descendant), but that pseudo-class does not distinguish keyboard focus from pointer focus the way :focus-visible does, so reusing it here would show the ring on a mouse click too; the minimal fix instead keeps the existing :focus-visible reach unchanged and only changes which property it sets, to a new NfcNavFocusRingShadow BoxShadow token (0 0 0 2 #60A5FA, same value in both themes, matching NfcAccentBorderStrongBrush) that coexists with :checked's underline instead of overwriting it.

Independent read-only review of exact head 6dee964a0 also found F-2 [P3]: this record's terminalContract first allowed HexEditor (no nav tab) to fall back focus to Home, then separately asserted the focused tab is always the one whose page is showing, which is false for that one page; the second sentence is corrected to name Home, Merge and Replace explicitly.

Second independent read-only review (codex/gpt-6-sol) of exact head 91214ef81 found F-3 [P2] by pixel-inspecting the before/after screenshots directly: the after screenshot for the focused-but-unselected tab had 0-13 matching #60A5FA pixels in the nav-bar region versus 380+ before the fix, so the BoxShadow property was set correctly but never reached the screen; the earlier report of '底線和焦點框同時可見' was not actually verified against rendered pixels. Bisecting a minimal reproduction (isolated ToggleButton with the real MainWindowStyles.axaml loaded) down to individual setters found the exact cause: giving PART_ContentPresenter a literal BorderThickness (even bottom-only 0,0,0,2, even on a sibling :checked rule, even with ClipToBounds=False on every ancestor) makes Avalonia's Border renderer clip a BoxShadow set on that same ContentPresenter to nothing; a bare ContentPresenter, or one with no BorderThickness, keeps the BoxShadow fully visible (reflection/rendering experiments against Avalonia 12.0.5, Rgba8888-format frame pixel sampling). ClipToBounds and RenderTransform were ruled out first and are not the cause.

Fix for F-3: PART_ContentPresenter no longer carries any BorderThickness in any ToggleButton.nav state; the selected-page underline moves to a new sibling Border.navSelectedUnderline (MainWindow.axaml wraps each nav ToggleButton in a Grid with that Border; the Border's IsVisible and the ToggleButton's own IsChecked are two independent OneWay bindings to the same IsHomeVisible/IsReplaceVisible/IsMergeVisible property, neither one driving the other), so the underline and the :focus-visible BoxShadow ring are two separate visuals that can never clip each other. The previous :checked:pointerover/:checked:pressed underline-color nuance on hover/press of the selected tab is dropped as a direct consequence (the underline is now a static Background bound only to selection, not a re-styled ContentPresenter border); decision 32 only requires the underline to be visible for the selected page, not that it change shade on hover/press of that same page, so this is a minor simplification, not a regression.

tests/NvtFwCombiner.UiSmoke.Tests/XamlControlStyleContractTests.Startup.cs CatalogWarmupUsesAccessibleRetryableForegroundLoadingSurface asserted the literal source strings for both the old focus-visible Border setters and the old unconditional HomeNavigationButton.Focus(NavigationMethod.Tab) call; both are updated to the new BoxShadow setter and the new SelectedNavigationButton(viewModel) call with its four explicit ShellPage arms. It also asserted the old :checked:pointerover/:checked:pressed ContentPresenter BorderBrush setters and the base ContentPresenter's BorderThickness, both removed by the F-3 fix; these are replaced with assertions on the new Border.navSelectedUnderline style and on the absence of BorderThickness anywhere in the nav ContentPresenter styles.

This record is re-admitted a second time only to move its integrationBase: PR #459 (batch 2b) merged into 1.1.x as e6e991af3 after the F-1/F-2 fix was first admitted, moving the latest valid evidence checkpoint to 241327de129cbbc1cd492070c3105ed91a03fe5f (docs: finalize the batch 2b records at the reviewed head); the branch was rebuilt onto origin/1.1.x at e6e991af3 by cherry-pick (git rebase --onto), not merge, and no nav-related file was touched by batch 2b.

Third independent read-only review (codex/gpt-6-sol) of exact head edd9a71b4 (full text in scratchpad/codex/NAVF3-last.md) confirmed F-3 closed by its own pixel check, and found three further findings, all FINDINGS-INCORPORATED-REQUIRED. F-4 [P2]: with a tab both selected and focused, Border.navSelectedUnderline's bottom edge sits directly against the :focus-visible BoxShadow ring's bottom bar; in the dark theme NfcAccentBrush and NfcAccentBorderStrongBrush both resolve to the identical #60A5FA, so the two bars read as one continuous line and the reviewer's own screenshot inspection agreed. F-5 [P2]: NavigationFocusIndicatorTests' HaloRegion sampled the full interior of the button, so the underline's own pixels could push the ring assertion over threshold without the ring actually rendering, and the region math used fixed pixel offsets rather than the control's own bounds, which does not hold at non-1x DPI. F-6 [P3]: no interactive test exercised (a) re-clicking the tab that is already selected, or (b) opening the navigation-clear confirmation and cancelling it, to confirm each nav tab's IsChecked still matches the real SelectedPage afterward.

Fix for F-4: Border.navSelectedUnderline gains Margin="0,0,0,3", holding its 2px bar 3px clear of the tab's own bottom edge where the focus ring is drawn, so the two bars never touch in either theme; verified by cropped/zoomed before/after screenshots showing a clean ring/gap/underline three-band separation in both light and dark themes. An unselected-but-focused tab still shows only the ring and no underline, so it cannot be mistaken for the selected tab; terminalContract is updated to state the gap explicitly.

Fix for F-5: NavigationFocusIndicatorTests.cs replaces the single interior HaloRegion/BottomEdgeRegion pair with three bounds-derived regions computed from each control's own Bounds and the window's RenderScaling (not fixed pixel coordinates, so the math holds at non-1x DPI): RingHaloRegion samples only the band directly above the control's outer edge (outside the button, where only the BoxShadow ring can paint); UnderlineRegion samples only the 2px band at bounds.Bottom minus the 3px gap minus the underline height (matching the F-4 margin); GapRegion samples the 3px band between them, inset horizontally by the same outset used for RingHaloRegion so the ring's own left/right side bars (which run the control's full height, including through the gap band near the corners) are not mistaken for gap bleed. Diagnosed the initial false-positive gap-region matches (3-6 stray pixels) by dumping raw pixel colors column-by-column, which showed the stray (96,165,250)/(175,210,252) values sitting only at the two side-bar columns, not in the middle, confirming the horizontal inset as the fix. Both tests assert GapRegion's matching-pixel count is exactly 0. Separately fixed CountColorPixels, which had been reading the rendered frame's bytes as BGRA (b,g,r from offsets 0,1,2); GetLastRenderedFrame() actually returns Rgba8888, confirmed by printing frame.Format and now asserted directly in the test (Assert.Equal(PixelFormat.Rgba8888, frame.Format)) so a future format change fails loudly instead of silently reading the wrong channels. Proved the rewritten regions actually discriminate ring-vs-underline, not just happening to pass, with a mutation test: temporarily zeroing NfcNavFocusRingShadow's alpha (ring invisible, underline untouched) made both RingHaloRegion assertions fail with 0 matching pixels while every UnderlineRegion and GapRegion assertion still passed, i.e. 'the ring disappears, the underline is still there' is exactly the failure the red evidence demonstrates; reverting the mutation restored all 8 tests to green.

Investigation for F-6 found a real, previously unknown defect, not just a test gap: MainWindowViewModel.Context.cs ApplySelectedPage(page) only raised OnPropertyChanged for IsHomeVisible/IsMergeVisible/IsReplaceVisible/IsHexEditorVisible inside its `if (pageChanged)` branch. A ToggleButton always flips its own IsChecked locally on click before any command runs; when the clicked page equals the current SelectedPage (ShellNavigationViewModel.NavigateToPage's existing early-return path already calls _bindings.ApplySelectedPage(page) for exactly this case), or when a pending navigation is opened and then cancelled (CancelNavigationClear closed the confirmation but never called back into ApplySelectedPage at all), pageChanged is false, so those four notifications never fired. Only the clicked-but-not-really-navigated tab's IsChecked could actually go out of sync: a ToggleButton always flips its own IsChecked locally on click, independent of any binding notification, so without that notification IsChecked kept showing the wrong tab as checked. Border.navSelectedUnderline's IsVisible has no such local-mutation path and stays bound to the same Is*Visible property, whose own value never changed in these two scenarios (SelectedPage itself never moved), so the underline was never actually wrong; the unconditional re-notification is what corrects IsChecked back to the value Is*Visible already held.

Fix for F-6: the four Is*Visible OnPropertyChanged calls in ApplySelectedPage move out of the `if (pageChanged)` branch to run unconditionally on every call, same-page or not (net zero line change in that file, since the same four calls are simply relocated, not duplicated). CancelNavigationClear in ShellNavigationViewModel.cs now calls the existing _bindings.ApplySelectedPage(_bindings.SelectedPage()) binding (no new binding/delegate added to ShellNavigationBindings) to force that same resync when a pending page switch is cancelled; because the page passed equals the current SelectedPage, pageChanged is false and only the unconditional notification path runs, consistent with the already-accepted same-page reclick behavior in NavigateToPage. New interactive tests (tests/NvtFwCombiner.UiSmoke.Tests/NavigationCheckedStateTests.cs), using the repo's real-click convention (Focus(NavigationMethod.Tab) + Space key press/release, not a direct Command.Execute), cover both scenarios end to end. Red evidence: reverting both call sites back to their pre-fix shape reproduced both failures verbatim -- 'Home's IsChecked drifted from the real selection after re-clicking its own tab.' and 'Home's IsChecked stayed stuck on 'checked' after the page-switch attempt to it was cancelled.' -- confirming the tests actually detect the defect, not just exercise the happy path; restoring the fix returned both to green alongside the full Navigation-filtered UiSmoke run.

MainWindowViewModel*.cs is capped in aggregate non-blank lines by tests/NvtFwCombiner.Architecture.Tests/RepositoryBoundaryTests.PresentationOrchestration.cs ShellNavigationOrchestrationUsesFocusedTypedChild at an owner-approved ceiling of 1024. Relocating the four existing OnPropertyChanged calls within MainWindowViewModel.Context.cs (rather than extracting a new helper method elsewhere in a MainWindowViewModel*.cs file) keeps this change's net contribution to that aggregate at zero, so the F-6 fix fits the ceiling without requesting an owner exception.

Fourth independent read-only review (codex/gpt-6-sol) of the F-4/F-5/F-6 head confirmed F-4 and F-6 closed, and that F-5's Rgba8888 fix and the ring's independent sampling region both hold (full text in scratchpad/codex/NAVF4-last.md). It found two further findings. F-7 [P2]: NavigationFocusIndicatorTests.cs's UnderlineRegion and GapRegion each rounded their own start/height independently (Floor for a start, Ceiling for a height), so their shared edge could disagree once RenderScaling is non-integer; the reviewer's own worked example (a control bottom edge at 50 logical px, scale 1.25) puts pixel row 58 inside both regions. F-8 [P3]: this record's own language read as if Border.navSelectedUnderline's IsVisible were driven by the ToggleButton's IsChecked, when MainWindow.axaml (lines 72/75, 82/85, 92/95) binds both independently, OneWay, to the same IsHomeVisible/IsReplaceVisible/IsMergeVisible property; and terminalContract's closing sentence claimed no non-startup navigation behavior changed in this record, which contradicted its own F-6 paragraph immediately above.

Fix for F-7: both regions now derive their one shared logical boundary (bounds.Bottom - UnderlineBottomGap) through one new PixelBoundary(logicalY, scale) helper (Floor(logicalY * scale)), so UnderlineRegion's end and GapRegion's start are the exact same computed integer at any scale, by construction, not by coincidence of the two formulas' independent rounding agreeing. Verified three ways: (1) NavigationFocusIndicatorTests.UnderlineAndGapBoundaryMathNeverOverlapsAtTheReviewersExampleScale is a plain (non-Avalonia) unit test reproducing the reviewer's own bottom=50/scale=1.25 example verbatim, asserting the pre-F7 formula's computed end/start do overlap there (proving the counter-example is real) and the new PixelBoundary-based formula's shared boundary is exactly equal; (2) Avalonia's headless window supports setting a non-integer RenderScaling directly (HeadlessWindowExtensions.SetRenderScaling, confirmed by reflecting Avalonia.Headless.dll and by an experiment showing a 1440x900 window's rendered frame becomes 1800x1125 pixels at scale 1.25 while control Bounds stay in logical units), so NavigationFocusIndicatorTests.UnderlineAndGapRegionsNeverOverlapAtAnyRenderScaling is a real [AvaloniaTheory] over scale in {1.0, 1.25} and both themes: it asserts UnderlineRegion.Y + UnderlineRegion.Height == GapRegion.Y structurally, and separately confirms real rendered pixels (ring, underline, zero-pixel gap) at each scale -- there is no remaining gap in non-1x rendering evidence, so no such limitation is recorded here; (3) manually reverting UnderlineRegion/GapRegion to their pre-F7 independent-rounding formulas and re-running the new scale theory did not reproduce a failure at this specific control's actual real-window bounds (the coincidence the fix does not rely on), which is why (1)'s reviewer-exact-numbers unit test carries the falsifying evidence rather than the live-rendering theory alone.

Fix for F-8: every place in this record that described Border.navSelectedUnderline's IsVisible and the ToggleButton's IsChecked is corrected to state they are two independent OneWay bindings to the same Is*Visible property, neither driving the other (MainWindow.axaml already wires them this way; only this record's prose was inaccurate). terminalContract's closing sentence is corrected to name F-6 as this record's one non-startup navigation-behavior change (ApplySelectedPage's unconditional Is*Visible re-notification and CancelNavigationClear's SelectedPage re-apply), instead of denying any such change existed.
semanticOwner: src/NvtFwCombiner.Presentation.Avalonia/Styles/MainWindowStyles.axaml remains the sole owner of ToggleButton.nav's visual states (base, pointerover, pressed, checked, disabled, focus-visible) and gains one new selector, Border.navSelectedUnderline, for the selected-page indicator; that indicator is now a dedicated sibling Border (declared per tab in MainWindow.axaml; its IsVisible and the ToggleButton's own IsChecked are two independent OneWay bindings to the same IsHomeVisible/IsReplaceVisible/IsMergeVisible property, neither one driving the other) instead of a BorderThickness/BorderBrush pair on the ToggleButton's own PART_ContentPresenter, which never carries a BorderThickness in any state so its :focus-visible BoxShadow ring can never be clipped by a co-located border stroke. Border.navSelectedUnderline also owns a fixed Margin="0,0,0,3" that keeps its bar a visible 3px clear of the ring drawn at the tab's own bottom edge, so the two never merge into one line in either theme (F-4). ThemeTokens.axaml remains the sole owner of the shared theme tokens and gains one new per-theme BoxShadows token (NfcNavFocusRingShadow) alongside its existing NfcWorkflowCardHoverShadow/NfcWorkflowCardPressedShadow tokens. MainWindow.axaml.cs remains the sole owner of startup focus restoration; it gains one private SelectedNavigationButton(MainWindowViewModel) helper, following the existing PageLabel(ShellPage) switch convention, that maps viewModel.SelectedPage to HomeNavigationButton, the newly named ReplaceNavigationButton, or MergeNavigationButton (both given x:Name in MainWindow.axaml, matching HomeNavigationButton's existing pattern). No other MainWindow.axaml.cs startup sequencing, ApplyLaunchPage, or ViewModel semantics changes. MainWindowViewModel.Context.cs's ApplySelectedPage(ShellPage) remains the sole owner of when the four nav Is*Visible properties are re-notified; ToggleButton.IsChecked and Border.navSelectedUnderline.IsVisible are two independent OneWay bindings to those same properties, so one re-notification keeps both in sync without either driving the other. That notification is now unconditional on every call, not only when the page actually changes, so a same-page reclick or a cancelled navigation attempt cannot leave a tab's checked state or its underline's visibility out of sync with the real SelectedPage (F-6). ShellNavigationViewModel.cs's CancelNavigationClear introduces no new binding; it reuses the existing ApplySelectedPage binding already in ShellNavigationBindings, calling it with the current SelectedPage to force that same resync when a pending page switch is cancelled.
terminalContract: Each nav ToggleButton (Home, Replace, Merge) is wrapped in a Grid with a sibling Border.navSelectedUnderline: a static 2px bottom bar in NfcAccentBrush, visible only when that tab's own IsHomeVisible/IsReplaceVisible/IsMergeVisible is true, unaffected by hover, pressed or focus state on either sibling, and held by a fixed Margin="0,0,0,3" 3px clear of the tab's own bottom edge. This sibling Border is the only 'selected page' indicator; the ToggleButton's own PART_ContentPresenter carries no BorderThickness in any state (checked, pointerover, pressed, disabled, focus-visible alike), because giving it one made Avalonia's Border renderer clip any BoxShadow on that same ContentPresenter to nothing (F-3). ToggleButton.nav:focus-visible draws a full 2px ring via BoxShadow (the NfcNavFocusRingShadow token, 0 0 0 2 #60A5FA in both themes) on PART_ContentPresenter, drawn just outside the tab's own bottom edge; because that ContentPresenter has no BorderThickness, the ring is never clipped and renders fully (verified by counting matching pixels in the rendered frame, not just reading the BoxShadow property back). A tab that is both selected and keyboard-focused therefore shows its underline (the sibling Border) and its ring (the ContentPresenter's BoxShadow) at the same time, on two independent visual elements, with a visible 3px gap between them in both the light and dark themes (F-4), so the two can never be mistaken for one continuous bar even where NfcAccentBrush and NfcAccentBorderStrongBrush resolve to the identical dark-theme #60A5FA; keyboard focus on an unselected tab never reads as a second selected tab, because shape, element identity and the gap all differ, not just color. Once the required startup stage succeeds, real keyboard focus (NavigationMethod.Tab, so :focus-visible applies) lands on whichever nav tab matches viewModel.SelectedPage at that moment: Home by default, or Merge/Replace when '--page merge'/'--page replace' (or another startup input) opened that page directly; a SelectedPage without a nav tab (HexEditor) still falls back to Home. Exactly one of Home, Merge and Replace is focused at startup; for HexEditor, Home is focused even though HexEditor's own page (not Home's) is the one actually showing. The selected tab's underline no longer changes shade on hover or press of that same tab (a minor simplification from removing the old BorderBrush-based mechanism; decision 32 does not require that nuance). Each nav tab's IsChecked and its underline's visibility -- two independent OneWay bindings to the same Is*Visible property, neither one driving the other -- always match the real SelectedPage after any click on it, including re-clicking the tab that is already selected, and including opening the navigation-clear confirmation by clicking a different tab and then cancelling it: neither binding leaves a tab showing as checked/underlined when it is not the actual SelectedPage, or vice versa (F-6). No nav brush token or other control's style changes. The one non-startup navigation-behavior change in this record is F-6 itself: ApplySelectedPage's four Is*Visible notifications are now unconditional (previously only on an actual page change), and CancelNavigationClear now re-applies the current SelectedPage, both described above; no other navigation behavior changes.
